cases.claimText: A failed UPI payment that was debited is reversed within 5-7 business days.
cases.citedSpan: Payments that are debited from the customer's account without a corresponding order are automatically detected by the nightly reconciliation job and reversed by the PSP within 5-7 business days.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: The reversal window is set by the PSP's dispute resolution process, not Ledgerly.
cases.citedSpan: This is not a Ledgerly-controlled window; it is set by the NPCI dispute resolution process that every UPI-enabled PSP must follow.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: You can check the UPI reference number against the transaction log.
cases.citedSpan: confirm the UPI reference number (a 12-digit UTR) and check whether ERR_UPI_COLLECT_FAILED or ERR_SETTLEMENT_DELAY appears against the transaction
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: A manual reversal is only needed if the automatic job has not caught it within 7 days.
cases.citedSpan: A manual reversal is only needed when the automatic job has not picked up the transaction after 7 business days, or when the customer disputes the amount reversed.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: The UTR is a 12-digit number visible in the bank statement.
cases.citedSpan: The UTR is a 12-digit number visible in the customer's bank statement and in payment-service's transaction log against the same order.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: UPI payments that are declined are usually due to insufficient balance.
cases.citedSpan: This usually means insufficient balance, an incorrect UPI PIN entered too many times, or the receiving VPA being temporarily suspended by the PSP.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Your refund of Rs 3,450 will be processed within 24 hours.
cases.citedSpan: A refund initiated through Ledgerly typically takes 5-7 business days to reflect in the customer's account once approved.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: ERR_UPI_COLLECT_EXPIRED means the request was not approved within the UPI window.
cases.citedSpan: the customer did not approve the request within the UPI-mandated window (typically 2 minutes on most apps)
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Settlement always takes exactly 2 days.
cases.citedSpan: Settlement is the process by which money collected via UPI, cards or netbanking actually lands in the merchant's bank account... typically T+2 working days.
cases.label: PARTIAL

cases.claimText: A bank holiday can extend the settlement window.
cases.citedSpan: A bank holiday extending the settlement window (settlement only happens on working days for the receiving bank, not the paying one).
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Ledgerly refunds are always issued to the original payment method within 3 days.
cases.citedSpan: A refund initiated through Ledgerly typically takes 5-7 business days to reflect in the customer's account once approved, matching the UPI reversal timeline.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: You should contact your bank directly for all refund enquiries.
cases.citedSpan: A refund initiated through Ledgerly typically takes 5-7 business days to reflect in the customer's account once approved.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: A downgrade is blocked if the account is using more team members than the target plan allows.
cases.citedSpan: Ledgerly blocks a downgrade from PRO or ENTERPRISE to a lower tier when the account is currently using a feature the target tier does not support -- most commonly more team members than FREE allows.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Historical data is retained even after a downgrade.
cases.citedSpan: Historical data, past invoices and exported reports are retained regardless of plan tier. A downgrade only affects what can be created or connected going forward.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: You can request a downgrade waiver from support for a one-time fee.
cases.citedSpan: The customer needs to remove the excess team members, disconnect the extra bank feed, or otherwise bring usage within the target plan's limits before the downgrade can proceed.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: ERR_2FA_MISMATCH is most often caused by the phone's clock being out of sync.
cases.citedSpan: The most common cause by far is the customer's phone clock being out of sync -- TOTP codes are time-based and a phone more than 30 seconds off will generate wrong codes consistently.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Resetting the authenticator app without re-scanning the QR code causes mismatches.
cases.citedSpan: the authenticator app may have been set up against a different account or re-installed without re-scanning the QR code, which silently generates a different code sequence.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: You can call our 24/7 support line at 1800-555-0134 for urgent 2FA resets.
cases.citedSpan: Resetting 2FA requires identity verification beyond a normal support interaction.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: 2FA reset requires identity verification beyond a normal support interaction.
cases.citedSpan: Resetting 2FA requires identity verification beyond a normal support interaction -- see the 2FA reset runbook.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: The rate limit is 100 requests per minute per API key on the PRO plan.
cases.citedSpan: api-gateway enforces 100 requests per minute per API key on PRO, and 500 per minute on ENTERPRISE.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: The limit applies per API key, not per calling process.
cases.citedSpan: the limit is per key, not per calling process, so five workers each making 30 requests a minute against the same key hit the PRO limit collectively.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: You should upgrade to ENTERPRISE immediately to fix this.
cases.citedSpan: api-gateway enforces 100 requests per minute per API key on PRO, and 500 per minute on ENTERPRISE.
cases.label: PARTIAL

cases.claimText: ERR_TALLY_CONN almost always means a network or Tally configuration issue on the customer's side.
cases.citedSpan: This is almost always a network or Tally configuration issue on the customer's side, not a Ledgerly outage.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: The sync connector's default port is 9000.
cases.citedSpan: Is the sync connector's configured port (default 9000) open on the local firewall?
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Tally sync happens every 5 minutes automatically.
cases.citedSpan: Is Tally actually running and the company file open on the machine running the Ledgerly sync connector?
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: ERR_GST_RECONCILE_FAIL is usually caused by a mismatched GSTIN.
cases.citedSpan: usually because of a mismatch between an invoice's recorded GSTIN and the one on the portal's records for the same transaction. A single-digit GSTIN typo is by far the most common cause.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: A reconciliation failure affects the underlying ledger entries too.
cases.citedSpan: A reconciliation failure affects only the GST return generation for the mismatched invoices specifically; it does not affect the underlying ledger entries, which remain correct regardless.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: KYC review typically completes within 24 hours.
cases.citedSpan: KYC document review is typically completed within 24 hours of a valid submission.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: The account cannot be accessed at all during KYC review.
cases.citedSpan: The account is fully created and accessible during KYC review; only specific actions ... are gated behind verification completing.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: A submission stuck beyond 48 hours should be escalated.
cases.citedSpan: A submission stuck beyond 48 hours with no rejection and no approval should be escalated -- this indicates the review queue itself has a problem.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: A GST return report over a full financial year can take up to 2 minutes.
cases.citedSpan: A GST return report over a full financial year with a high transaction volume can take up to 2 minutes -- this is expected, not a fault.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Splitting a large export into monthly chunks avoids the timeout.
cases.citedSpan: Splitting a large export into smaller date-range chunks (monthly instead of annual, for instance) avoids the timeout and is the standard workaround.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: Ledgerly guarantees 99.99% uptime under its SLA.
cases.citedSpan: A single occurrence, resolved by narrowing the date range, does not need escalation.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

cases.claimText: You will receive a credit for any downtime automatically.
cases.citedSpan: A single occurrence, resolved by narrowing the date range, does not need escalation.
cases.label: NOT_SUPPORTED
